headline: Napoli 'too fragile' as unbeaten Roma come to Naples
summary: Napoli beat Bodo/Glimt 4-3 on Tuesday, their first Champions League win of the season, yet Max Allegri still called his side 'too fragile' — and they have conceded seven goals in their last two home European games. On Saturday they host Roma, third in Serie A and unbeaten with 17 points. The last five meetings are level: two Napoli wins, one for Roma, two draws. Italian media report Paulo Dybala is out for Roma, and that Lorenzo Pellegrini's injury complicates Gasperini's choices behind the striker. The market makes Roma narrow favourites, 37.8% to Napoli's 34.4%, with over 2.5 goals at 50.9%.

sources.fact: Napoli director Giovanni Manna said coach Max Allegri 'is absolutely not in doubt' and that president Aurelio De Laurentiis wanted to be 'reassured' after two defeats, ahead of the Bodo/Glimt match.
Napoli beat Bodo/Glimt 4-3 in the Champions League, their first win of this season's competition.
Scott McTominay scored twice in the 4-3 win over Bodo/Glimt, his first goals since a procedure for a minor cardiac arrhythmia that kept him out for a month.
Allegri said after the 4-3 win that Napoli were 'too fragile' but that Kevin De Bruyne 'is going to really enjoy himself playing in front of the defence'.
Napoli lost 1-0 away to Venezia in Serie A, part of the run of two defeats that preceded the Bodo/Glimt win.
Sky pundit Ugolini wrote that, missed penalty aside, De Bruyne doesn't seem to have 'the attitude of someone who made the right choice in coming to Napoli'.
Roma beat Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Olimpico for their first Champions League victory of the season, with goals from Hermoso, Molina, Pisilli and Malen.

Italian media report that Roma are without Paulo Dybala and that Pellegrini's injury complicates Gasperini's attacking-midfield choices, while Bryan Cristante's return is a positive sign after his knee problem.
